clue.text: Hospital dismisses retiring type

parts.note: a san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for dismisses is read backwards

parts.note: to dismiss staff is to fire them

explanation.surface: A hospital lets go of an employee who is shy and withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like a kind of person, retiring and shy, but it is the printer's sense: a typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanserif is a typeface whose letters lack the small finishing strokes, so it is a style of printing type.

clue.text: Loyalty is lacking for instance in union

indicators.note: is lacking says the abbreviation for 'for instance' goes missing from the loyalty word

parts.note: allegiance is loyalty to a ruler or cause
e.g. is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: A partnership falls apart because one side lacks loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lacking' removes EG from ALLEGIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or association formed for mutual benefit, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Most deficient examinations

parts.note: a scan is a medical examination
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A doctor laments the poorest set of check-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, and its superlative describes whatever is most lacking or meagre.

clue.text: British not taking part in frenzied attack

indicators.note: not taking part says the letter for British drops out of the frenzied word

parts.note: rabid means wildly frenzied or fanatical

explanation.surface: Britain stays out of a wild military assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not taking part' removes B from RABID.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden attack, as by troops or police, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Cool guy talked of letters from admirers

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it with a moving current of air

indicators.note: talked of says the word for guy is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a guy is a male person

explanation.surface: A laid-back man chats about the letters he has received from fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' is a verb here, giving FAN; 'talked of' turns MALE into its sound-alike MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fan mail is the correspondence a celebrity receives from admirers.

clue.text: New version of Kes makes it as a musical

indicators.note: a new version reworks the material, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Kes is a 1969 British film, used here as letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remake of the film Kes turns it into a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New version of' rearranges KES MAKES IT. Kes is a 1969 British film about a boy and his kestrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiss Me, Kate is a Cole Porter stage musical based on The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Be sick on getting to school, turning a pale colour

indicators.note: turning means the whole run of pieces is read from the end backwards

parts.note: to ail is to be ill
taken as written
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A child feels ill on arriving at school and goes pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses AIL + ON + GAM as one run. GAM, a school of whales, is crossword vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnolia is a creamy off-white shade named after the flower, popular as a pale paint colour.

clue.text: Cotton fabric worn by any number inhabiting Greek island

indicators.note: inhabiting says the pieces live inside the island's name

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island
a garment that is on someone is worn by them
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A cotton fabric is worn by countless residents of a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretonne is a heavy printed cotton cloth used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Man having a lean look

parts.note: a ship that lists leans to one side
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A man has a thin appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean' is a verb here, not an adjective meaning thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Alistair is a man's first name, and crosswords often use 'man' to define a name.

clue.text: European outlaw I caught in a way, out east

indicators.note: caught in says the pieces are held inside the road word
out says the compass letter leaves the road word

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way or road
E is the compass abbreviation for east
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A European bandit is captured on a road heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out east' looks like a direction of travel, but it tells you to drop the compass letter from the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An Albanian is a native of Albania, a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: He composed religious music in Spanish and French

parts.note: a Mass is a musical setting of the Eucharist liturgy
en is Spanish for in
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A composer writes church music in two languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Massenet was a French composer of operas such as Manon, so he is a man who composed.

clue.text: Company's record is very curious, you say

parts.note: to enter details is to record them

indicators.note: you say signals that the word for being very curious is heard spoken, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: someone who pries is nosily curious

explanation.surface: A firm's track record is remarkably odd, people remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you say' turns PRIES into PRISE, which follows ENTER. The 's after Company stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a business undertaking, so it can stand for a company or firm.

clue.text: No end to writing a dissertation? This one may supply missing part

definitions.text: This one may supply missing part

indicators.note: no end to says the last letter of the writing word is removed

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
a thesis is a dissertation

explanation.surface: An academic who never finishes a dissertation needs help with the missing chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole sentence: 'This one' points at the answer itself, an artificial part that replaces a missing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is an artificial body part, such as a false limb, that replaces one which is missing.

clue.text: Scheme to penetrate swamplands

indicators.note: to penetrate means a word is found buried inside the next word

explanation.surface: A plan to drain the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to penetrate' finds the word inside swamPLANds.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or design for doing something, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Member of film crew rather young for role at wedding?

definitions.meaning: on a film set, the chief assistant to the gaffer or key grip

definitions.text: rather young for role at wedding?
definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: the best man at a wedding, if he were only a boy

explanation.surface: A film technician seems too young to stand beside the groom.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: the best man's job taken by a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A best boy is the chief electrician's or grip's assistant in a film crew, credited at the end of films.

clue.text: Concede defeat, being in lower division once more?

definitions.meaning: to yield or withdraw from a position under pressure

definitions.text: being in lower division once more?
definitions.meaning: a team relegated again is literally returned to a lower division

explanation.surface: A football club gives up when relegated yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: To back down is to withdraw a claim or concede; read literally the words say returned downwards again.

clue.text: To speak about son of God's not hard … here?

definitions.text: To speak about son of God's not hard … here?

indicators.note: about says the speaking word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to say is to speak

indicators.note: not says the letter for hard is left out of the holy name

parts.note: Christ is the Son of God in Christian belief
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A worshipper reflects that speaking about Christ is easy in a church room.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a church room where one might speak about Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristy is the room in a church where sacred vessels and vestments are kept, a place to speak of Christ.

clue.text: In English town servicemen recalled fighting

indicators.note: In says one piece sits inside the town's name

parts.note: Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire, England

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, whose members are servicemen

explanation.surface: Airmen are called back to a town in England as conflict breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare is the waging of war, the activity of fighting between armed forces.

clue.text: Excessively head over heels in love affair of little consequence

indicators.note: in says the turned word sits inside the affair word

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair

indicators.note: head over heels means turned upside down, so in a down clue the word is reversed

parts.note: too means excessively

explanation.surface: Someone madly in love has a brief romance that means little.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'head over heels' turns a word upside down, which reads it from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Footling means trivial or petty, of little importance.

clue.text: Means of controlling resistance that rose The Times after revolution

indicators.note: after a revolution things are overturned, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A device controlling dissent became popular when The Times backed a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' rearranges THAT ROSE; 'The Times' adds only to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to adjust electrical current by changing resistance.

clue.text: Brought into line, wearing clothes

definitions.meaning: soldiers are ... when aligned in formation

explanation.definitionFit: Dressed has a military sense of aligned in ranks as well as the everyday sense of clothed.

clue.text: Source of drug, oddly cool chap

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the words

explanation.surface: A drug comes from a strangely relaxed fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks C, O, C, A from cool chap.
explanation.definitionFit: The coca shrub's leaves are the source of cocaine.

clue.text: Having considered carefully, reversed position

explanation.definitionFit: To turn something over is both to ponder it and to flip it, so the phrase fits each sense.

clue.text: Bristled furiously, given tiny amounts to drink

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drinker bristles with rage when served only tiny sips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' rearranges BRISTLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Driblets are small drops or trickles of liquid, tiny quantities.

clue.text: Stone work on middle section of wall

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: middle section of means the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Masonry is placed in the middle of a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle section of' takes AL from wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone, so it is a precious stone.

clue.text: Son expresses preference about his teachers

indicators.note: about says the preference word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to opt is to choose or express a preference

explanation.surface: A boy states which of his tutors he likes best.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sophists were paid teachers of rhetoric and philosophy in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Wife takes a moment to consume last of the sorbet

indicators.note: to consume says the moment phrase swallows the final letter

parts.note: a trice is a moment, as in 'in a trice'

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A wife takes a moment to finish the last of her sorbet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes E from 'the', not from sorbet, which is the definition; 'to consume' puts E inside A TRICE, after W.
explanation.definitionFit: A water ice is a frozen dessert of flavoured syrup, much like a sorbet.

clue.text: Representative has appointment to be shown round European circuit

indicators.note: shown round says the date word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a date is an appointment
a leg is one lap or stage of a circuit

explanation.surface: A delegate has a meeting and is taken round a European tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a person sent to represent others, such as at a conference.
